categoryName: Snacks & namkeen — chips, extruded, bhujia, popcorn

skuLines.line: Potato chips — national brand, ₹5/₹10 impulse pack
skuLines.examples: Lay's Magic Masala 23-25g, Uncle Chipps Spicy Treat, Bingo Original Style, Balaji Simply Salted
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; collapses during school winter/summer vacation, peaks at session start and exam weeks
skuLines.marginBand: 8-15% (national impulse packs sit at the bottom of the kirana band)
skuLines.notes: The single highest-rotation line in the whole category. Nitrogen pillow packs are almost all air — huge volumetric freight per rupee up 30-50 km of hill road, and crush loss is real. Order in original outer cartons, never loose sacks. Shelf life 3-4 months; monsoon humidity at 173101 makes soggy returns the main write-off.

skuLines.examples: Lay's India's Magic Masala 52-58g, Bingo Original Style 72g, Uncle Chipps 53g, Balaji Chaat Chaska
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes on weekends and hostel movie/match nights
skuLines.notes: The workhorse price point for university students with pocket money. Same crush/volume constraint as impulse packs.

skuLines.examples: Lay's Party Pack 157g, Bingo Mad Angles Party Pack, Balaji Crunchex 135-140g
skuLines.seasonality: Festivals (Diwali, Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Hola Mohalla), staff-family gatherings, birthdays, sports day
skuLines.notes: Better freight economics per gram than impulse packs. Balaji-type regional wafer brands give far more grammage per rupee and carry the best margin of the branded set (16-20%).

skuLines.line: Potato chips — plain / lightly salted, low-spice
skuLines.examples: Lay's Classic Salted, Balaji Simply Salted, Bingo Salted, Pringles Original
skuLines.notes: Non-negotiable for a township with married staff and toddlers plus some elderly — the masala SKUs are too hot for both cohorts. Usually the first line a store under-stocks and the first complaint it hears.

skuLines.line: Potato wafers — regional value brand, high grammage per rupee
skuLines.examples: Balaji Wafers, Yellow Diamond, Shyam-G, local Punjab/HP wafer packers
skuLines.notes: Where the store actually earns in this category. Regional packers give 18-25% and negotiate scheme support; freight from Punjab/Gujarat depots is the constraint, so buy in full-load quantities before monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Lay's Wafer Style, Bingo Original Style Chilli Sprinkled, Balaji Crunchex
skuLines.notes: Thicker cut survives hill transport measurably better than thin-sliced chips — worth over-indexing here relative to a plains store.

skuLines.examples: Pringles Original / Sour Cream & Onion / Peri Peri 102-107g, Lay's Stax
skuLines.notes: Rigid cans show materially lower damage claims than pouches across a 4-7 handling chain — the format best suited to 30-50 km of hill road. Premium price limits it to staff and senior students; check the veg mark on imported flavours.

skuLines.examples: Bingo Potato Chipsticks, Aloo Sticks, Balaji Aloo Sev
skuLines.notes: Doubles as a topping for chaat/bhel at the canteen counter — cross-sells with the F&V side.

skuLines.examples: A1 Chips, Flavours of Calicut, Beyond Snack, loose Kerala chips
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; higher in winter with tea
skuLines.notes: Real pull from South Indian university students and staff. Coconut-oil fried, so rancidity is the risk: 2-3 month practical shelf life and it turns fast in monsoon humidity. Buy small, rotate hard.

skuLines.examples: Kerala sarkara upperi, Flavours of Calicut jaggery chips
skuLines.notes: Jaggery coating gets sticky in high humidity — needs airtight storage; not a monsoon line.

skuLines.examples: Kerala tapioca chips, vacuum-fried jackfruit chips, mixed veg chips
skuLines.notes: Vacuum-fried versions keep much better than pan-fried; the ₹250/pack tier is a staff-only price in this township.

skuLines.line: Premium root/veggie chips (beetroot, sweet potato, multi-veg)
skuLines.examples: Cornitos Veggie Chips, 4700BC veggie crisps, Yoga Bar-tier veg chips
skuLines.notes: Thin list only — one or two facings. Low velocity in a school township; buy on q-commerce-style small MOQs, not depot loads.

skuLines.line: Extruded masala sticks — the ₹5/₹10 volume engine
skuLines.examples: Kurkure Masala Munch 25g/36g, Bingo Tedhe Medhe Masala Tadka, Kurkure Chilli Chatka
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; academic-calendar driven, dead in vacations
skuLines.notes: Along with ₹5/₹10 chips this is the top-two velocity line for a 5,000-person campus. Denser and far less crush-prone than potato chips, so it travels the hill road well. Shelf life 4-6 months.

skuLines.examples: Kurkure Puffcorn Yummy Cheese 28g, Cheetos Masala Balls 84g, Lehar Puffcorn
skuLines.notes: Melt-in-mouth texture and low chilli make this the safest savoury for 5-10 year olds and toddlers — the line the crèche/married-quarters cohort asks for by name. Extremely bulky: worst freight-per-rupee in the category, order full outers.

skuLines.line: Corn rings / fryum rings with toy inside
skuLines.examples: Crax Corn Rings, Crax Crunchy Pipes, Piknik rings
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes after pocket-money day and on visiting Sundays
skuLines.notes: The toy is the purchase driver for under-12s — a closed campus with no alternative shop makes this near-guaranteed rotation. Baked not fried, so a slightly easier line to defend on a school shelf.

skuLines.examples: Crax Sweet Rings (chocolate / strawberry / mango)
skuLines.notes: Sits between snack and confectionery; keep 2 flavours, not the full range.

skuLines.examples: Crax Fryumms Classic Salted, Yellow Diamond Wheels, Pasta Green Chilli fryums
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin extruded sub-segment and cheapest per gram. Also stock raw un-fried fryums by weight for staff families who fry at home — that is a separate, better-margin decision.

skuLines.examples: Cornitos Nacho Crisps 30g/60g/150g, Doritos Cheese/Nacho, Act II nachos
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks on match nights, hostel-room parties, staff get-togethers
skuLines.notes: Cornitos ladders neatly at ₹20/₹35/₹85 so you can serve student and staff wallets from one brand. Robust chip — travels well. Check veg mark on imported Doritos variants.

skuLines.examples: Cornitos salsa/cheese dip, Veeba, Del Monte, Chings
skuLines.notes: Only worth stocking beside the nachos facing. Cheese dips want a cool shelf — feasible in a cold hill location, but check 'refrigerate after opening' before selling to hostellers with no fridge.

skuLines.line: Baked corn / millet puffs (jowar, ragi, bajra)
skuLines.examples: Kurkure Jowar Puffs, Too Yumm Multigrain Chips, ragi/bajra puffs
skuLines.notes: The one line that lets a school-run store answer the HFSS/junk-food question without losing the sale. Several states now restrict HFSS sale within 50 m of school premises and require an FSSAI licence for canteens — a baked millet shelf is the compliant substitute, and worth a labelled 'healthier snack' bay.

skuLines.examples: Act II RTE, 4700BC Instant/Classic, Cornitos popcorn
skuLines.notes: Extremely bulky and fragile — the worst crush and volumetric-freight profile in the lane. Best answered locally: pop on campus from kernels rather than trucking air 50 km.

skuLines.examples: 4700BC caramel/cheese, Act II Tomato Chatka, gourmet flavoured popcorn
skuLines.seasonality: Festivals, sports day, annual function, birthdays
skuLines.notes: Caramel goes sticky and stale fast in monsoon humidity — small, frequent orders only.

skuLines.examples: Act II butter/classic 70-80g, 4700BC Pop Box 80g
skuLines.notes: Only sells to households that own a microwave — married staff quarters, not hostels. Long shelf life (9-12 months) and compact, so it is one of the few popcorn formats worth trucking in bulk.

skuLines.examples: Loose maize popping corn, 4700BC kernels, Act II kernels
skuLines.notes: Cheapest cost per serve in the whole category, 12-month shelf life, compact freight — the correct hill-logistics answer to popcorn demand and the input for an on-site popping counter.

skuLines.examples: Bikaji Bikaneri Bhujia 1kg ₹299, Haldiram's Bhujia 42g ₹10 / 200g / 400g
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; strong winter tea-time lift, festival peak
skuLines.notes: The anchor namkeen for a Punjabi/North-Indian population. Stock both the ₹10 impulse pack and a 1kg family pouch — different buyers. Besan-fried, so 3-6 month shelf life and it turns rancid faster in warm damp storage; keep the ₹10 packs moving and the 1kg on airtight display.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Aloo Bhujia, Bikaji Aloo Bhujia, BTW 850g, Shyam-G
skuLines.notes: Milder than Bikaneri bhujia, so it is the family-and-elderly workhorse. Pairs with the tea/rusk shelf.

skuLines.line: Sev — nylon, plain, garlic, Ratlami, Indori
skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Nylon Sev, Ratlami Sev, garlic sev, Indori sev
skuLines.notes: Doubles as a chaat/bhel input for the canteens — stock a 1kg institutional pouch alongside the retail pack so the canteen does not have to buy retail.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Moong Dal, Bikaji Moong Dal, Shyam-G
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; festival and Gurpurab langar-adjacent lift
skuLines.notes: Low-chilli and widely acceptable across ages — one of the few namkeens elderly residents buy repeatedly.

skuLines.examples: Bikaji Chana Dal, Haldiram's Chana Dal
skuLines.notes: Twin of moong dal; carry both but do not multiply pack sizes on each.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Khatta Meetha, Bikaji Khatta Meetha
skuLines.notes: Sweet-sour profile makes it the mixture children accept; consistently in the top 3 namkeen SKUs nationally.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Navratan Mix, Bikaji Navratan, Bombay Mixture 1kg
skuLines.notes: The default 'guests are coming' namkeen for staff quarters.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Chivda, cornflake chivda, dry-fruit chivda, Gopal chivda
skuLines.notes: Lighter-fried and lower-spice; also the base a store can buy in bulk and repack at 25-40% margin (needs FSSAI licence and own-label declaration to do legally).

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Dal Biji 200g, Bikaji Dal Moth
skuLines.notes: North-Indian staple; one facing is enough.

skuLines.line: Chana jor garam / flattened spiced chana
skuLines.examples: Chana Jor Garam, Banarasi-style chana
skuLines.notes: Cheap, dense, travels perfectly (no air, no crush) — an unusually good hill-logistics SKU.

skuLines.line: Falahari / vrat mixture (no onion, no garlic)
skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Falahari Mixture, Bikaji Falahari, sabudana chips
skuLines.notes: A Sikh institutional township needs a clearly-marked onion-garlic-free shelf. Every SKU in this lane must be 100% vegetarian green-dot — no gelatin, no animal-derived enzymes or flavourings, which is the specific risk in imported chips and cheese-flavour seasonings.

skuLines.line: Punjabi mathri / mathi / namak para / shakarpara
skuLines.examples: Local Punjab mathri, Haldiram's Mathri, namak para, shakarpara
skuLines.seasonality: Strong winter peak with tea; festivals, Lohri, Baisakhi
skuLines.notes: The regional line residents would otherwise drive 30-50 km to buy. Best sourced from a Punjab packer or made on campus; 15-30 day fresh shelf life if locally made, so it is a fast-rotation, high-margin, low-freight decision.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Bhakarwadi, Chitale, Gopal
skuLines.notes: Draws Maharashtrian and western-India staff/students; one SKU.

skuLines.examples: Gopal Gathiya, Balaji Gathiya, Induben chorafali
skuLines.notes: Very fragile and bulky — arrives broken if handled loose. Buy in cartons.

skuLines.examples: Grand Sweets-style murukku, Haldiram's Chakli, kodubale, thenkuzhal
skuLines.notes: Real demand from South Indian university students and faculty who have no other source within 30-50 km. Highly breakage-prone; rigid secondary packaging matters.

skuLines.examples: Mukharochak Chanachur, Haldiram's Chanachur, jhalmuri mix
skuLines.notes: One or two SKUs to serve eastern-India residents; Mukharochak and Haldiram both distribute nationally.

skuLines.examples: Induben Khakhrawala, Stuti Khakhra, Haldiram's khakhra
skuLines.notes: Roasted not fried, low oil, 4-6 month shelf life — the best 'parent-approved' tiffin snack and a natural fit for the healthier-snack bay. Breaks easily: needs box packs, not pouches, for hill transport.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Soya Sticks 200g, Stuti soya sticks, Induben 150g
skuLines.notes: High-protein positioning sells itself to hostel students and gym-going staff. Dense, robust, long shelf life — a good hill SKU.

skuLines.line: Ready-to-eat fried savouries — papdi, mini samosa, dry kachori, matthi
skuLines.examples: Haldiram's mini samosa, dry kachori, papdi, matar (dried peas)
skuLines.notes: Short shelf life (1-3 months) and oil-heavy — buy small and often, or make on campus at the canteen and sell fresh at a much better margin.

skuLines.line: Bhel / chaat ready mix + papdi kit
skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Bhel Puri kit, bhel mix + tamarind/green chutney sachets
skuLines.notes: Cross-sells hard with the F&V counter (onion, tomato, coriander, lemon) — the one snack line that lifts a different department's basket.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Masala Peanut, Bikaji Masala Peanut, Jabsons
skuLines.notes: Himachal's own namkeen tradition is peanut-led (masala peanut, pahadi mixture) — this is a local-taste must, not an add-on. Long shelf life, dense, ships well.

skuLines.examples: Jabsons roasted peanuts, Nutraj, loose bhuna moongphali
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy winter peak in a cold hill location
skuLines.notes: Cheapest protein snack on the shelf and the single best loose-weigh line for a hill store: no crush risk, no air freight, 6-9 month shelf life, margin set by you not by an MRP.

skuLines.examples: Bhuna chana, chana masala, roasted black chana
skuLines.notes: The school-approved snack: no fry, no maida, high protein. Ideal for a hostel/canteen bulk indent and for the healthier-snack bay.

skuLines.examples: Too Yumm Makhana (Tandoori/Peri Peri) 20-25g ₹20, Farmley Makhana 200g ₹230, Bikano makhana
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; fasting days and festive gifting peak
skuLines.notes: Fastest-growing 'good-for-you' snack in India and already at a ₹20 impulse price point. Very light and bulky — freight per rupee is poor, but value density is high enough to absorb it. Keeps 6-9 months if sealed; goes chewy the moment it meets monsoon air.

skuLines.examples: Too Yumm Multigrain Chips 45g ₹20, Too Yumm Veggie Stix, Dahi Papdi Chaat
skuLines.notes: Baked, no-palm-oil, lower-saturated-fat claims — the credible answer when parents or the school ask what the store sells children. Not a replacement for chips; national data shows both shelves grow together.

skuLines.examples: Protein puffs, roasted lentil crisps, high-protein namkeen with front-of-pack claims
skuLines.notes: Thin facing for gym-going staff and senior students. New-brand-heavy segment discovered on q-commerce first — buy small trial quantities.

skuLines.line: Salted / spiced cashew & premium nut namkeen
skuLines.examples: Spicy cashew, masala kaju, Jabsons flavoured nuts, kaju mix
skuLines.notes: Staff and visitor-gifting line only; keep inventory tight — highest rupee-per-unit write-off risk in the lane.

skuLines.line: Papad — ready-to-roast and roasted masala papad snack
skuLines.examples: Lijjat papad, moong/urad papad, masala papad, papad fryums
skuLines.notes: Classed with namkeen in Indian retail and a kitchen staple for every married-quarters household. Extremely humidity-sensitive at a heavy-monsoon hill site — needs sealed storage or it softens and cannot be roasted.

skuLines.examples: Chana madra mixture, pahadi masala peanut, local Sirmaur/Solan packers
skuLines.notes: Sourced within Himachal, so the freight problem disappears and margin is negotiated not fixed. This is the differentiated line no national brand supplies and no resident can get elsewhere without a trip to town.

skuLines.examples: Lay's multipack of 5, Kurkure multipack, Bikaji sweets+namkeen combo, Haldiram value pack
skuLines.seasonality: Session start (parents stocking a hosteller), festivals, birthdays, annual function
skuLines.notes: Session-start and visiting-day is the highest-intent buying moment on this campus — a parent dropping a child for a term buys a month of snacks at once. Better freight economics than the same grammage in singles.

skuLines.line: Institutional bulk namkeen & chips for canteens
skuLines.examples: 1kg namkeen pouches, 3-5kg bhujia/sev/chivda sacks, bulk fryums, bulk peanuts
skuLines.priceBand: ₹150-₹400/kg (₹160-₹300/kg wholesale on sev, soya, chana lines)
skuLines.notes: Two canteens, a warehouse and an Ary Lite counter should be buying on internal indent, not off the retail shelf. Bulk is also the cheapest way to move namkeen up a hill road — one 5kg sack instead of 125 air-filled 40g pillows.

skuLines.examples: Bhujia, sev, chivda, mathri, peanuts, roasted chana weighed out at 250g/500g
skuLines.notes: The highest-margin decision in the whole lane and the one that lets residents buy ₹20 of what they want instead of a fixed MRP pack. Requires an FSSAI licence, own-label declarations (name, ingredients, veg mark, packing/expiry date, batch) and airtight bins — at 173101's monsoon humidity, uncovered loose namkeen is a two-week write-off.

trends2026: Millet snacking went mainstream, not niche — jowar/ragi/bajra puffs and chips from national players (PepsiCo's Kurkure Jowar Puffs) riding the government's 'Shree Anna' push; millet SKUs now appear in q-commerce, school tiffins and corporate snack boxes, not just health stores.

Makhana became the breakout savoury format: flavoured roasted foxnut in ₹20 impulse packs through to ₹230/200g branded tubs, positioned on ~15g protein per 100g; reported as a go-to 'superfood' snack for 3 in 5 Indian consumers.

Protein-forward savoury — front-of-pack protein claims on chips, puffs, soya sticks and roasted lentil/chana; consumers are actively label-reading for low-fat and high-protein rather than buying on flavour alone.

Korean and global heat flavours crossed over from K-drama/K-pop into real preference among 18-30s: Korean chilli, Korean BBQ, sweet-spicy umami, plus peri-peri and chilli-oil crunch appearing on mainstream Indian chip lines.

Baked / air-fried and 'no palm oil, less saturated fat' as an explicit shelf position (Too Yumm's whole platform), sitting alongside indulgent chips rather than replacing them — households buy healthier on weekdays and indulgent on weekends.

Barbell pricing: the ₹5-₹30 band still anchors ~60% of the snack shelf, while premium ₹60-₹130 nachos, canister chips and gourmet popcorn grow fastest in value — a store needs both ends, not a middle-only range.

Channel-specific pack architecture — brands now run different grammages and price points for general trade vs quick commerce, with faster replenishment cycles; new brands get discovered on apps first and reach kirana shelves later.

Regulatory pressure on the kids' shelf: multiple states (Maharashtra FDA order of 28 July 2026, Karnataka, Rajasthan HC direction of Aug 2026) restrict HFSS sale and promotion within 50 m of school premises and mandate FSSAI licensing for canteens — pushing school-linked retail toward baked, millet, roasted-chana and fruit alternatives, and driving reformulated lower-spice, cleaner-label kids' snacks.
adjacentServices: Canteen and hostel bulk-indent supply — sell 1-5 kg institutional packs of sev, bhujia, chivda, peanuts, fryums and popcorn kernels to the two canteens and Ary Lite on internal indent instead of letting them buy off the retail shelf.

On-campus popping and frying counter — pop popcorn from ₹100-200/kg kernels and fry fryums/papad fresh, instead of trucking air-filled RTE pouches 30-50 km; converts the worst freight line in the category into the best margin.

Loose-weigh namkeen bar — bulk-buy bhujia, sev, chivda, mathri, peanuts and roasted chana and weigh to order at 250g/500g, at 25-40% margin instead of a fixed MRP; needs FSSAI licence and own-label declarations.

Session-start and visiting-day snack bundles — a parent dropping a hosteller for a term is the highest-intent buyer on campus; pre-built ₹300/₹500/₹1000 term boxes and parent-funded student snack wallets capture it.
Festival and gifting hampers for Diwali, Gurpurab, Baisakhi and Hola Mohalla — namkeen + dry-fruit + mathri boxes for staff, visiting families and institutional gifting.

A labelled 'healthier snack' shelf endorsed by the school — baked millet puffs, khakhra, roasted chana, makhana, plain popcorn — the compliant answer to state HFSS-near-schools rules and to parents' questions.
Local Himachali packer sourcing — contract a Sirmaur/Solan packer for pahadi mixture, masala peanut and mathri: no long-haul freight, negotiated margin, and a range no resident can buy elsewhere.

Pre-monsoon stock-up and pre-order window — take indents and pre-position 2-3 months of dense, long-shelf-life snacks (kernels, peanuts, chana, chana jor garam, soya sticks, microwave popcorn) before hill-road access becomes unreliable in Jul-Sep.

Airtight storage and humidity-controlled bins as a paid-for capability — at PIN 173101's monsoon humidity, sealed storage is what keeps papad, khakhra, bhujia and loose namkeen sellable rather than written off.

Wrapper and multilayer-plastic take-back in a closed township — a collection point for snack packaging keeps the campus clean and answers EPR/plastic-waste obligations that a 5,000-person closed community will otherwise carry alone.
